body: Silent Bomber is CyberConnect's PlayStation action game, first released in Japan on 28 October 1999. Jutah infiltrates the enormous space dreadnought Dante, attacking its defences with remotely detonated bombs. The player can place explosives nearby or launch them onto a target, then decide when to trigger the blast. This separates aiming from firing in an unusual way. An enemy can already be marked for destruction while the player moves elsewhere, making the timing of the explosion as important as the accuracy of the initial placement.

Bombs can be stacked to increase their destructive power, while destroying several enemies together rewards a chain. Only a limited number can remain active at once, so detonating a group also makes room for the next attack. Special materials add effects: napalm leaves burning ground, gravity draws enemies together and paralysis disrupts machinery. The player chooses how to arrange these effects around moving opponents. Instead of simply holding a firing direction, an encounter becomes a quick plan about which targets to mark and when the whole arrangement should explode.

The camera and movement recall a top-down shooting game, but its bomb system gives combat a rhythm of placement, repositioning and detonation. That sequence makes the player responsible for both preparing an attack and recognising the right moment to complete it. Chikayo Fukuda and Seizo Nakata composed the score. Silent Bomber followed Tail Concerto as CyberConnect's second game, before the company became CyberConnect2. North American and European releases arrived in 2000, carrying a compact and distinctive action design into the later years of the original PlayStation.
